visual_notes: Existing drawings use dark brown/black outlines and transparent negative space; some cream fills. New set can be simpler true monochrome but should not become hard-edged icons.
Bhukha already has a large imagined drum illustration, so a second drum adds less narrative information and would require separate instrument-specific reference for any new details.
Existing illustration is a style/composition reference only, not historical or cultural proof.

proposals.motif: A modest household courtyard and open threshold
proposals.source_section: A house made ready for a family
proposals.evidence: The director recalled preparing an abandoned Puri house and courtyard as the only set with a small crew and nonprofessional performers.
proposals.documented_vs_symbolic: House/courtyard documented; exact architecture, door and light arrangement are invented editorial symbols, not a reconstruction.
proposals.prompt: Poetic Natural monochrome line-art vignette for a nonfiction book. A few restrained graphite-black ink lines suggest one plain open doorway and a shallow strip of household courtyard, seen slightly obliquely. A narrow angled shadow crosses the threshold, the rest dissolves into generous transparent negative space. No people, ornate pillars, religious motifs, broken masonry, film equipment, text or border. Quiet human scale and plausible perspective. This is an imagined threshold accompanying a family-film essay, not a film still or actual Puri house. Wide horizontal composition; selective hand-drawn lines, no filled grey background.
proposals.placement: After final narrative paragraph in A new encounter with the family, before Watch and explore.
proposals.alt: A simple drawn doorway opens into a quiet courtyard.
proposals.avoid: Do not turn abandoned-house recollection into picturesque decay or claim this exact doorway appears in the film.

proposals.motif: Unlettered rolled publicity sheets and one partial screen edge
proposals.evidence: Mohapatra described posters, banners and promotion as separate distribution expenses; reaching local audiences is part of the chapter’s ending.
proposals.documented_vs_symbolic: Publicity materials documented in director testimony; arrangement next to screen is symbolic, not an actual screening scene.
proposals.prompt: Poetic Natural black ink line drawing, wide transparent vignette. Two loosely rolled, unlettered paper publicity sheets lie slightly overlapping near a very lightly suggested corner of a small projection screen; one sheet partly unrolls towards the screen. Focus on the work of bringing a film to viewers. Economical irregular strokes, generous empty space, no text, faces, posters with pictures, instruments, tickets, coins, ornate village architecture or border. No distressed paper effects. Symbolic editorial art, not a reconstructed event.
proposals.placement: After closing narrative paragraph in Following the filmmaker forward, before Watch and explore.
proposals.alt: Rolled publicity sheets beside the lightly drawn edge of a cinema screen.
proposals.avoid: Do not repeat the existing drum hero or introduce an unverified instrument subtype, costume or performance scene.

proposals.motif: Two ordinary chairs and a closed document folder
proposals.evidence: Official Film Bazaar synopsis describes household employment insecurity, retirement, debt and illness.
proposals.documented_vs_symbolic: Household and job-waiting premise documented; chairs/folder are explicitly symbolic objects, not attested film props.
proposals.prompt: Poetic Natural monochrome ink vignette on transparent background. Two plain household chairs seen from a slight side angle, one nearer than the other, with a closed unlettered paper document folder resting on the nearer seat. Spare, quiet lines and a little floor contour, no full room. The distance between chairs carries waiting and family dependence. No hospital bed, medicine, death symbolism, government seal, forms, words, portraits or border. Physically plausible furniture, not decorative antique styling; wide low composition. An imagined illustration, never an exact film scene.
proposals.placement: After final paragraph linking the household’s uncertainty with the economics chapter, at chapter tail.
proposals.alt: Two simply drawn chairs, with a closed folder resting on one seat.
proposals.avoid: No implication that a specific employment file or these chairs appear in Pratikshya. Do not make a father/son tableau without viewing evidence.

proposals.motif: Two people’s hands sharing the weight of a plain closed field case
proposals.evidence: The film’s origin account foregrounds workers reaching distant villages; chapter explicitly restores teams and volunteers to the doctor-centred story.
proposals.documented_vs_symbolic: Collective outreach and access difficulty documented; exact case and handover are symbolic, not actual programme equipment or film action.
proposals.prompt: Poetic Natural black ink line-art vignette, transparent wide horizontal composition. Cropped forearms and two ordinary hands from opposite sides jointly support the bottom of one small closed plain rectangular carrying case. A short understated uneven ground contour below suggests travel. Hands bear the weight naturally; no floating box and no impossible grips. No faces, white coats, stethoscopes, red crosses, medicine labels, syringes, tribal costume or heroic raised gestures. Sparse lines and generous negative space; a symbolic image of care carried together, not a medical procedure or film still.
proposals.placement: After final narrative paragraph of Returning to the film, before Watch and explore.
proposals.alt: Two hands share the weight of a closed carrying case.
proposals.avoid: Do not depict patients, imply local residents are passive, or authenticate this invented case as programme equipment. If hands look contrived, simplify rather than add a heroic doctor.

placement_rules: Keep all existing images and their attribution.
Use tail ornaments after substantive prose; do not force a new page solely for line art.
Keep the vignette with enough preceding prose to avoid an isolated decorative leaf; prefer about160–180pt width and natural aspect ratio, with maximumheight determined by actual layout.
No new factual footnote needed for imagined object arrangement; retain internal symbolic provenance and accessible descriptive alt text. Public art treatment follows existing editorial policy.
Root must inspect generated anatomy/perspective and the final book spread; prompts are directions, not proof of output quality.
limits: No film viewing or new visual historical research in this pass.
Specific objects in Pratikshya and DAMaN are symbolic and not verified props.
No copied poster or still, actual portrait, religious iconography or inferred costume proposed.
